originalTitle: Like Trump, Pauline Hanson plays the media and attacks the media simultaneously. Who’s using who? | Zoe Daniel
summary: One Nation is borrowing heavily from the Maga playbook. But constant claims of being misquoted predate the US president’s
content: Time to call a spade a spade. One Nation’s rise is the media’s fault. And Pauline Hanson being misunderstood is also the media’s fault. Elements of the media have amplified the rise of One Nation over three decades, with outsized coverage normalising what is now a populist machine. At the same time, Hanson treats the media as her enemy. Can both things be true? The first is a deliberately provocative statement. The second is an observation. Both lead to questions about the media’s role and responsibility in an era of information manipulation. The phrases “fake news” and “enemy of the people” come to mind in these times when it appears that whatever the question is for Hanson, Donald Trump is the answer. The latest example relates to her comments about violence against women in which she makes excuses for violent men. “It is wrong but it’s also a two-way street,” she told the Brisbane radio station 4BC. “I’m not saying that it’s just men, women can lose their cool as well. Society is under so much pressure … Everyone is under so much pressure and it’s really hard.” The facts are that intimate partner violence is overwhelmingly perpetrated by men. She went on to say that women who are being abused should just leave: “If these women are getting abused by men out there, then don’t put up with it.” The data also shows that leaving is the most dangerous time for women and children. The remarks have caused an outcry which has provoked Hanson to again claim that her comments have been misrepresented. “Here’s exactly what I said on 4BC about domestic violence, so you don’t get it twisted by the media or the Labor Party,” she posted on social media. “There is a concerted effort by some in the media to constantly take my comments out of context.” It could not be more Trumpian as she plays the media and attacks the media, simultaneously. In 2016, Trump was estimated to have received as much as US$5.9bn in free media coverage, more than doubling Hillary Clinton’s presence in the press, while underspending her official campaign on his way to victory in the 2016 presidential election. At the same time, he dominated social media, simultaneously vilifying and bypassing the mainstream media to build an audience he could communicate with directly, while sucking the legacy media into temptation chasing the ratings he could command. Sound familiar? When I was the US bureau chief for the ABC in 2016, US television networks hung on Trump’s every word, broadcasting hours of live, unchecked diatribes. By the time the factcheckers properly mobilised it was too late. The post-truth era was already upon us. Factchecking no longer landed with the average person. Trump had become all but untouchable. The media had become the enemy of the people and anything remotely critical was labelled fake news. Eroding trust in the media was crucial to his strategy. One Nation is now borrowing heavily from this playbook. Hanson’s gaslighting over the White Australia policy, “no good Muslims”, paid parental leave and now violence against women mirrors Trump’s tactics; making statements then walking them back or denying she made them at all. While she’s taken the predictable approach of arguing that the “left-wing media” has twisted her words in “false clickbait stories”, it’s not true. Her recent remarks follow a long pattern of behaviour. In her maiden parliamentary speech in 1996 she said: “I believe we are in danger of being swamped by Asians.” That was before she told the Greens senator Mehreen Faruqi to “pack your bags and piss off back to Pakistan”, which led to a federal court finding of unlawful racial discrimination and vilification under the Racial Discrimination Act. Yet parts of the media continue to facilitate her rise, while appearing surprised and disturbed that it’s happening. Channel Seven’s Spotlight program was snookered by Hanson’s team when it either participated in or helped organise her trip around Europe, in which she met rightwingers and hung out in Italy with Gina Rinehart. Seven denies arranging the meetings while, surprise, surprise, Hanson has accused the program of misrepresenting its intentions. That said, the network got the ratings. Conspiracy theorists might suspect that the argy-bargy was confected to achieve that. Who knows? The mainstream media is losing influence as consumers increasingly get their news from social media, which is forcing legacy organisations to feed the algorithm to survive. But the more Hanson is freely platformed as clickbait rather than properly scrutinised, the more likely it is that One Nation will find its way to power. And who will take responsibility for that? Zoe Daniel is a three-time ABC foreign correspondent and the former independent member for Goldstein
chineseTitle: 和特朗普一样，宝琳·汉森一边玩弄媒体，一边攻击媒体。谁在利用谁？ |佐伊·丹尼尔
chineseSummary: 一国党大量借鉴了马加的剧本。但在美国总统发表讲话之前，不断有人声称被错误引用。
chineseContent: 是时候实话实说了。一国党的崛起是媒体的错。 Pauline Hanson 被误解也是媒体的错。三十年来，媒体元素放大了“一国”的崛起，超大报道使现在的民粹主义机器正常化。与此同时，汉森将媒体视为她的敌人。这两件事都可以是真的吗？第一个是故意挑衅性的言论。第二是观察。两者都引发了人们对媒体在信息操纵时代的角色和责任的质疑。当汉森遇到什么问题时，“假新闻”和“人民的敌人”这两个词就会浮现在脑海中，唐纳德·特朗普就是答案。最新的例子与她对暴力侵害妇女行为的评论有关，她在评论中为暴力男性找借口。 “这是错误的，但它也是一条双向街道，”她告诉布里斯班广播电台 4BC。 “我并不是说只有男人才会这样，女人也会失去冷静。社会承受着很大的压力……每个人都承受着很大的压力，这真的很难。”事实是，亲密伴侣暴力绝大多数是由男性实施的。她接着说，受到虐待的女性应该离开：“如果这些女性在外面受到男性的虐待，那就不要忍受。”数据还显示，离开是妇女儿童最危险的时期。这些言论引起了强烈抗议，汉森再次声称她的言论被歪曲了。她在社交媒体上发帖称：“这正是我在 4BC 上所说的关于家庭暴力的内容，所以你不会被媒体或工党歪曲。” “一些媒体齐心协力，不断断章取义地解读我的言论。”这简直就是特朗普式的
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
